cards.title: "Mujhe kuch nahi hua hai"
cards.body: Many parents push back on medicines. Arguing louder rarely works. Understanding why they're refusing usually does.

cards.title: Ask why, then actually listen
cards.body: Side effects, cost, too many tablets, or a fear of getting "used to" medicines. Each reason needs a different answer.

cards.title: Take side effects seriously
cards.body: If a medicine makes them feel unwell, tell the doctor. There may be other options. Just don't let them stop it on their own.

cards.title: Make the routine simpler
cards.body: Lots of tablets at odd times is exhausting. Ask the doctor or pharmacist whether the routine can be made easier.

cards.title: Bring the doctor in
cards.body: Sometimes parents hear it better from their doctor than from their child. Go to the visit together and let them ask their own questions.

cards.title: Respect, don't police
cards.body: They're adults who raised you. Offer help and information, not threats. Pressure mostly teaches people to hide skipped doses.

cards.title: Patience is part of care
cards.body: Keep the conversation open, keep the doctor informed, and keep showing up. Most minds change slowly.

takeaway: When parents refuse medicines, find out why, tell the doctor, and simplify the routine instead of arguing.
